title: Sine and cosine rule
cover_sub: Trigonometry for triangles without a right angle. Secure choosing the right rule, extend to areas and contexts, then master the ambiguous case and algebra.

levels_long.s: Sine rule, cosine rule and ½ab sin C, one step each.
levels_long.e: Angles, quadrilaterals, contexts, and tampered evidence.
levels_long.m: Two possible triangles, bearings, and forming equations.

briefing: Label the sides with lower-case letters opposite their angles: side a is opposite angle A.
Sine rule (a pair of opposite side and angle, plus one more): asin A = bsin B = csin C. Cosine rule (two sides and the angle between, or all three sides): a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A. Area = ½ab sin C.
method: Label the triangle: angles A, B, C; sides a, b, c opposite them.
Have you got a side and its opposite angle? Sine rule. Otherwise, cosine rule.
Substitute, then rearrange before you press any buttons.
Round only at the end, and check the biggest side is opposite the biggest angle.

example.question: In triangle PQR, PQ = 9 cm, PR = 7 cm and angle P = 50°. Find QR.
steps: Two sides and the angle between them, with no opposite pair: cosine rule.
QR = √49.01 = 7.00 cm. Check: it's opposite 50°, between the other two sides ✓

text: In triangle ABC, b = 7 cm, c = 9 cm and angle A = 50°. Find a.
Find the area of a triangle with sides 6 cm and 9 cm and an angle of 40° between them.
A triangle has sides 7 cm, 8 cm and 9 cm. Find the largest angle.
questions.tip: The largest angle is opposite the longest side. Rearrange first: cos C = (a² + b² − c²) ÷ 2ab.

text: In triangle ABC, a = 10 cm, angle A = 70° and b = 8 cm. Find angle B.

e.blurb: A step is hidden, or there's a context to unpick. One piece of tampered evidence.

text: Two observers are 200 m apart on a straight road. They see a suspect's drone at angles of 50° and 60° from the road. How far is the drone from the first observer?
questions.working: The third angle is 70°. 200 sin 60° ÷ sin 70°.
questions.tip: Sketch it first. The side you want is opposite the angle at the second observer.

text: A triangle has sides 5 cm, 6 cm and 7 cm. Find its area.
questions.working: Find one angle by the cosine rule (e.g. 78.5° between 5 and 6), then ½ × 5 × 6 × sin 78.5°.

text: A parallelogram has sides of 8 cm and 5 cm, with angles of 60° and 120°. Find the length of its longer diagonal.
In triangle XYZ, XY = 12 cm, angle X = 35° and angle Y = 80°. Find XZ.
Jas used the cosine rule with b = 7, c = 9 and A = 50°. Find her mistake.
questions.working: She multiplied the whole of b² + c² − 2bc by cos A. Only 2bc is multiplied by cos A.

m.blurb: No hints. Plan before you calculate.

text: In triangle ABC, a = 7 cm, b = 9 cm and angle A = 40°. Find the two possible sizes of angle B.
questions.working: sin B = 9 sin 40° ÷ 7 = 0.826. The second angle is 180° − 55.7°.
questions.tip: When the side opposite the known angle is the shorter one, two triangles can fit. Check whether 180° minus your angle also works.

text: A triangle has an area of 30 cm². Two of its sides are 8 cm and 10 cm. Find the acute angle between them.
questions.working: ½ × 8 × 10 × sin C = 30, so sin C = 0.75.

text: A patrol boat sails 12 km on a bearing of 060°, then 8 km on a bearing of 130°. How far is it from its start?
questions.working: The angle at the turn is 180° − 70° = 110°. d² = 144 + 64 − 192 cos 110°.

text: A triangle has sides x cm, (x + 1) cm and (x + 2) cm. The largest angle is 120°. Find x.
Show that the area of an equilateral triangle with side s is (√3/4)s².

closed_points: Label any triangle and choose between the sine and cosine rules.
Find missing sides and angles in triangles without a right angle.
Find the area of any triangle with ½ab sin C.
Spot the ambiguous case and give both angles.
Use the rules with bearings and with algebra.
